audiences.language: Use consumer platform names in marketing copy.

audiences.description: A person who recognizes protocols, engines, and connection modes.
audiences.language: Use exact engine and protocol names. Include technical detail only when it changes a decision.

needs: Separate implemented behavior from roadmap work
audiences.language: Use precise implementation and release terms.

attributes.name: Clear
attributes.write: Name the subject, action, and result.
attributes.avoid: Metaphors, unexplained implementation terms, and sentences that need a second read.

attributes.name: Calm
attributes.write: State what happened and give the next action.
attributes.avoid: Alarm, blame, jokes during failures, and exaggerated reassurance.

attributes.name: Direct
attributes.write: Address people as you. Use imperative verbs for actions.
attributes.avoid: The user, one can, you will need to, and indirect instructions.

attributes.name: Specific
attributes.write: Name the affected platform, connection, engine, or capability.
attributes.avoid: Something went wrong, unsupported operation, and vague qualifiers.

attributes.name: Honest
attributes.write: Separate available, preview, in-development, and planned work.
attributes.avoid: Coming soon without a date, implied availability, and unsupported privacy claims.

attributes.name: Human
attributes.write: Use familiar verbs and contractions where they sound natural.
attributes.avoid: Spec-sheet voice, corporate filler, and forced friendliness.

notOurVoice: Dense networking jargon in primary flows
Absolute claims about anonymity, safety, speed, or privacy

style.address: Use you for the reader. Use RahRow for the product.
style.tense: Use present tense unless a sentence describes future behavior.
style.steps: Start instructions with an imperative verb.

sentenceLength.rule: Rewrite longer sentences when one reading does not reveal the action and result.

style.paragraphs: Keep one idea and no more than four sentences per paragraph.

headings.rule: Use descriptive, user-shaped headings. Avoid Overview, Notes, and Caveats.

lists.rule: Convert three or more parallel items into a list.
lists.introduction: Introduce every list with a complete sentence ending in a colon.
lists.unordered: Use bullets when sequence does not matter.
lists.ordered: Use numbers for steps or lifecycle order.
lists.punctuation: Omit periods from fragments. Keep periods on complete sentences.

punctuation.emDash: Do not use em dashes as punctuation. Use a colon, comma, or new sentence.
punctuation.ellipsis: Use … for loading and omitted text. Do not use three periods.
punctuation.ampersand: Use and in prose. Use & only in a space-constrained interface label.
punctuation.quotes: Use curly quotation marks in rendered prose. JSON syntax requires straight quotation marks.

formatting.bold: Reserve bold for interface labels and critical facts.
formatting.code: Use inline code for paths, file extensions, commands, identifiers, and literal values.
formatting.links: Use destination-specific anchor text. Do not use here, link, or a bare URL.
formatting.sourceParagraphs: Do not hard-wrap prose paragraphs in Markdown source.

style.acronyms: Spell out a specialized acronym on first use. VPN may remain abbreviated on constrained marketing and interface surfaces.
style.contractions: Use contractions for warmth when they remain clear.
style.we: Use we only for a deliberate project decision. Do not use we as a substitute for you.
style.questions: Do not use rhetorical questions. Use questions only when RahRow requires an answer.

banned.reason: These words pressure the reader and replace a concrete explanation.
These words make vague or unverifiable claims.
A client cannot guarantee these outcomes.

titleRules: Keep the title specific and under eight words when possible.
Do not expose an error code as the title.
Do not blame the person or provider.
descriptionRules: Explain the consequence in plain language.
Include technical detail only when it changes the next action.
Do not promise that retrying will work.
diagnosticRules: Put technical codes and native capability names in expandable details.
Preserve exact engine and platform names.
Make logs copyable without making them the primary message.

brand: The copy identifies RahRow as a client, not a service.
The canonical headline and description remain unchanged when used as the brand lockup.
accuracy: Every platform claim matches current release evidence.
Every protocol claim distinguishes implemented work from roadmap work.
Every engine claim matches the engines included in the artifact.
VPN and proxy mode remain distinct.
The copy makes no unsupported privacy, anonymity, security, or speed claim.
voice: The copy uses active voice and direct address.
Each sentence names a clear subject and action.
The tone stays calm during errors.
The copy avoids filler, pressure words, jargon, and rhetorical questions.
structure: The opening paragraph explains what the surface covers.
Headings use sentence case and describe their sections.
Paragraphs contain one idea and no more than four sentences.
Lists use the correct order and punctuation.
interface: Buttons begin with clear action verbs.
Loading states use the ellipsis character.
Errors include a working next action when one exists.
Unavailable states do not imply automatic fallback.
Technical details stay secondary to the user-facing message.
metadata: The title names RahRow and the page purpose.
The description states a concrete action or capability.
The slug uses lowercase words separated by hyphens.
Download language appears only for released artifacts.

reviewOutput.fileReviewFormat: Group findings by file and use file:line - issue → correction.

reviewOutput.requiredDisclosure: List factual assumptions that could not be verified.
